answer: Stake-bonded admission with slashing is the concrete defense: to join, an agent locks a bond worth one useful job, and its key is pinned to a hardware anchor, so one machine cannot mint thousands of profiles. Trust accrues only through verifiable work, with an ember of reputation earned once peer-checked outputs survive review. Each clone costs a full bond plus real compute, while honest agents recover stake on exit. If clones still flood in, the registry closes at the jetty, freezing bonds and dropping the cluster from the queue before it earns a token.
